newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to get briefing on UPS from labor secretary.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to get briefing on UPS from labor secretary.

text.p: Labour Secretary Alexis Herman will brief President Clinton on the United Parcel Service strike as the two fly to St. Louis Tuesday for a presidential speech, the White House said.

White House spokesman Mike McCurry said he was not aware of any progress in the strike at Atlanta-based UPS, which before the strike delivered about 80 percent of all packages shipped by ground nationwide.

He said Herman had been scheduled to travel with Clinton to St. Louis, where he will talk about efforts to move people from welfare to work, a topic that falls within the concerns of the Labour Department.
"She was scheduled to go anyhow but she's going to give the president a little briefing on the plane," McCurry told reporters before Clinton's helicopter took off from the White House lawn.
Asked if there was any progress to report, McCurry replied: "No. She put out a statement last night. They are continuing to try to urge the parties to negotiate."
UPS and Teamsters union representatives met Herman Monday but there were no signs of a break in the 9-day-old strike.
"I made it clear that everyone involved must show greater flexibility and a willingness to compromise," Herman said Monday, describing the meetings as serious but offering no indication of progress.
Teamsters President Ron Carey told reporters after his meeting with Herman that he was ready to go back to the bargaining table, but only for serious negotiations.

UPS negotiator Dave Murray said the firm was not changing its offer despite Herman's calls for flexibility. "We still believe that the correct solution to this is for the Teamsters to put our people back to work and send our offer out for a vote," Murray said.
